scores.reasoning: Multi-factor authentication is on, but the recovery email is a departed staff member's personal address, which the firm does not control.
Transfer lock is on for both domains at the registrar.
The registry offers registry lock and it is not enabled on either domain.
Auto-renew is off on both domains; the main domain expires in about four months.
The two main domains are listed with owner and purpose, but a second registrar account holds two domains that appear on no list.
Two-step verification is on for both logins, and only the two administrators who manage the zones have access.
DNSSEC was never enabled: no DNSKEY records and no DS records.
The provider logs zone changes, but nobody reviews the log.
The parent's nameserver records match the zone's own and both nameservers answer authoritatively.
Two nameservers, but both sit in the DNS provider's single network.
Whether either nameserver refuses an outside zone transfer has never been tested.
No copy of either zone's records is kept outside the DNS provider.
One SPF record within the lookup limit, but it still names a marketing platform the firm stopped using in 2024.
The SPF record ends in a soft fail (~all), with no dated step toward -all.
The mail platform signs with 2048-bit keys; the invoicing tool sends unsigned.
DMARC has been at p=none since 2023, with no dated step toward enforcement.
Aggregate reports go to a mailbox nobody reads; the unread reports go back to 2023.
Neither the sp nor the np tag is published.
The parked domain sends no mail and publishes no SPF and no DMARC record.
The sender mapping has never been re-checked: the SPF record still includes the marketing platform dropped in 2024.
No MTA-STS record or policy is published.
No TLS-RPT record is published.
No CAA record is published, so any certificate authority may issue for the domains.
Whether the mail platform supports DANE has never been checked.
No subdomain inventory exists.
help.wrenfield.example still points at the helpdesk service the firm left in 2024.
projects.wrenfield.example is delegated to a former web vendor's nameservers, unchanged and unreviewed since 2022; who operates them now is unknown.
One wildcard exists; its reason is only half remembered and nothing records it.
